### Discovery & Translational Science

*   **Depp1 identified as a key regulator of muscle atrophy** [DOI 10.64898/2026.09.21.753276]
    *   Research indicates Depp1 is induced in skeletal muscle during nutrient or oxygen limitation via FoxO1 and HIF pathways, respectively; Depp1 overexpression is sufficient to mediate muscle atrophy in mice.
*   **Role of CRTC2/3 in osteoblastic gene expression confirmed in vivo** [DOI 10.64898/2026.09.21.753306]
    *   Conditional deletion in osteoblast lineages showed transient effects on bone mineral density and structure in male mice; findings highlight regulation of *Rankl*, *Runx2*, and *Sost* expression.
*   **TSG-6 deficiency linked to delayed wound healing in T2DM** [DOI 10.64898/2026.09.19.752893]
    *   Study in diabetic mice shows that reduced TSG-6 expression exacerbates inflammation; exogenous TSG-6 protein re-introduction improved healing and normalized cytokine levels.
*   **Novel pan-cancer classifier for childhood tumors** [DOI 10.64898/2026.09.23.26355605]
    *   Development of FRANK (Fully-connected RNA-based Augmentation Neural Klassifier), a neural network trained on 11,467 transcriptomes, achieving 98.3% accuracy across diverse pediatric tumor types.

### Early Trials — Phase I–II

*   **[Biotech] RNAZ reports stabilization in Phase 1a trial** [X / Twitter]
    *   Ongoing Phase 1a study of TTX-MC138 shows continued disease stabilization and extended treatment duration.
*   **[Biotech] ACET posts positive data for Prula-cel in SLE** [X / Twitter]
    *   At 12 months, 54% of evaluable patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (with or without lupus nephritis) achieved DORIS remission, with 50% achieving clinical response.

### Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

*   **[Biotech] Mirum Pharmaceuticals meets primary endpoint in Phase 3 study** [X / Twitter]
    *   The AZURE-1 study of brelovitug met its primary endpoint in chronic hepatitis delta virus (HDV) patients.
*   **[Biotech] Kodiac hits primary endpoints in wAMD pivotal trial** [X / Twitter]
    *   The DAYBREAK trial for Zenkuda and tabirafusp-ted in wet age-related macular degeneration met primary endpoints (p = 0.0007); 54% of patients achieved efficacy on a 6-month dosing interval.

### Regulatory & Approvals

*   **[Big Pharma] AbbVie secures FDA approval for Parkinson’s treatment** [STAT / X / Twitter]
    *   FDA approved Juvmo (tavapadon) as a once-daily oral treatment for Parkinson’s disease.
*   **[Big Pharma] Merck and Daiichi withdraw ifinatamab deruxtecan application** [BioPharma Dive / X / Twitter]
    *   Companies pulled the BLA for accelerated approval of the antibody-drug conjugate in small-cell lung cancer after the FDA indicated Phase 2 results were insufficient; a separate late-stage trial is ongoing despite recruitment issues.

### Business & Strategy

*   **[Big Pharma] Merck licenses KRAS inhibitor in $400M deal** [X / Twitter]
    *   Merck entered a global licensing agreement with SciBrunch Therapeutics for the preclinical oral KRAS G12D (ON) inhibitor SPR2015 for $400M upfront.
*   **[Big Pharma] Roche discontinues CDK4 inhibitor** [X / Twitter]
    *   Roche confirmed the termination of the ex-Regor CDK4 inhibitor program (RG6795).
*   **[Biotech] Scynexis awarded BARDA contract** [X / Twitter]
    *   Company received a contract providing up to $214M in non-dilutive funding for the development of SCY-247.

### Public Health & Policy

*   **Trump administration cuts HHS funding** [STAT]
    *   Administration clawed back nearly $1 billion in previously approved spending, specifically targeting HHS programs focused on diversity and immigrants.
*   **Rising mortality in encephalopathy** [DOI 10.64898/2026.09.21.26363584]
    *   Analysis of U.S. death records (1999–2024) reveals a 28.4% increase in age-adjusted mortality, with notable demographic disparities and a surge in cases classified as "unspecified."
*   **Partner-inflicted brain injuries in women** [DOI 10.64898/2026.09.24.26363984]
    *   Study of 207 survivors suggests repeat partner-inflicted brain injuries are associated with cognitive aging, with impaired patients performing a decade older than non-injured survivors.

**Worth watching:** The increasing trend of marketing GLP-1 agonists as "lifestyle" drugs for customers rather than obesity treatments for patients, and the growing focus on "operational talent" in biopharma as specialized manufacturing challenges complicate drug delivery.

- Biology & Health
    - [4 Ways to Melt Visceral Fat!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jaYMmt7E79Q) -- Physionic
        - The video outlines four distinct options for reducing visceral fat based on scientific literature.
        - References include clinical studies on therapeutic peptides like GLP-1 receptor agonists and tesamorelin.
        - Other cited interventions involve dietary strategies, fasting protocols, and resistant starch.
    - [409 ‒ Inside modern drug development: the science, economics, and regulatory hurdles](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GoNjdK-I0Bc) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Lloyd Klickstein explains the modern drug development arc, spanning unmet medical need identification, target selection, animal testing, and clinical trials.
        - Bimagrumab serves as a case study for targeting myostatin and activin signaling to increase muscle mass and strength.
        - Early clinical trials revealed unexpected improvements in fat mass and type 2 diabetes, leading to its development for obesity, including combination trials with semaglutide.
        - The discussion covers drug modalities (biologics vs. small-molecule therapeutics), patents, capital allocation, IND submission requirements, and GMP manufacturing.
    - [The nuances of diagnosing and treating thyroid dysfunction | Peter Attia, M.D.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/TM90xQSGxHI) -- Peter Attia MD
        - The episode examines the two core thyroid laboratory tests routinely checked on every patient, alongside expanded workups for specific clinical situations.
        - It highlights that the normal range for TSH increases with age, preventing the misdiagnosis and overtreatment of older adults.
        - Standard blood tests for free T3 and free T4 are noted as being least reliable when diagnostic accuracy is most critical.
        - The discussion addresses managing mildly elevated TSH with otherwise normal panels, addressing residual symptoms on T4 therapy via T3 addition, and the impact of food on thyroid medication absorption timing.
